nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Short northern summers set the growing season for the forest, bogs and alpine heath.

nodes.name: Rain, fog and snow
nodes.desc: Moisture from the Gulf of St. Lawrence and a snowy winter shape the plants that grow here, from forest to coastal bog.

nodes.name: Peat and poor soils
nodes.desc: Bogs on the coast are rich in peat, and the ultramafic Tablelands have stony, nutrient-poor soil. Plant growth is limited by what the ground supplies.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen trees, leaf litter and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Balsam fir
nodes.desc: The common conifer of Newfoundland forests, and a winter browse for moose, hares and caribou. Its seeds and buds feed squirrels and others.

nodes.name: Tamarack
nodes.desc: A deciduous conifer of bogs and wet ground. Moose, hares and voles eat its shoots and bark.

nodes.name: Bunchberry
nodes.desc: A low forest-floor plant with red berries, eaten by hares, voles, caribou and bears.

nodes.name: Labrador tea
nodes.desc: An evergreen shrub of bogs and heath. Caribou, hares and voles nibble it.

nodes.name: Meadow vole
nodes.desc: A small grassland and bog rodent that eats plant shoots and seeds. It is a staple prey for foxes and martens.

nodes.name: American red squirrel
nodes.desc: Feeds on conifer seeds and buds and is taken by lynx, fox and marten.

nodes.name: Snowshoe hare
nodes.desc: A browser of twigs, buds and low shrubs, and the main prey of the lynx.

nodes.name: American beaver
nodes.desc: Cuts trees for food and dams, creating ponds that other wildlife use.

nodes.name: Newfoundland caribou
nodes.desc: An ecotype of caribou found in the park. It grazes lichens and low plants, and calves can be taken by bears.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: Introduced to Newfoundland around 1900, it now reaches densities five to 20 times those in comparable areas. It browses fir, tamarack and other plants.

nodes.name: American marten
nodes.desc: The Newfoundland form is threatened. A forest hunter of voles, hares and squirrels, and itself prey of the red fox.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: An opportunist that hunts hares, voles, squirrels and martens and scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A scavenger that feeds on carcasses of moose and other animals.

nodes.name: Canada lynx
nodes.desc: A cat that hunts mainly snowshoe hares, and also takes squirrels and foxes. It is a top predator of the park.

nodes.name: Black bear
nodes.desc: The Newfoundland form is a large omnivore that eats berries and also takes moose and caribou calves.
